personal.title: Frontend Developer
personal.bio: With 5 years of experience as a frontend developer, I design and ship high-performance web experiences with React, Next.js, and TypeScript—bridging design systems, accessibility, and measurable Core Web Vitals gains.

about.title: Building interfaces that feel fast and intentional
about.p1: I specialize in React and Next.js product work—design systems, performance budgets, and the craft details that make complex UIs feel simple. I partner closely with design and backend teams to ship durable frontend architecture.

projects.title: Selected work
projects.description: Shipped product UI, a shared component kit, and performance-first surfaces from recent roles.

proj-01.title: Nova Design System
proj-01.shortDescription: The team's source-of-truth React kit—tokens, primitives, and docs that replaced one-off UI across four products.
proj-01.fullDescription: Built Nova as a versioned React + TypeScript package so product squads stopped restyling the same button. Primitives (dialog, combobox, data table, form controls) map 1:1 to Figma, ship with Storybook, and are typed so a token change is a single package bump instead of a repo-wide hunt.
responsibilities: Shipped 20+ typed primitives with compound APIs, variants, and design-token theming.
Wired Storybook + a11y addon into CI so keyboard traps and contrast failures blocked merge.
Made every interactive primitive WCAG AA: focus order, ARIA, and reduced-motion paths.
Migrated two legacy apps onto Nova and cut duplicated UI styles by more than half.

proj-02.title: Pulse Analytics
proj-02.shortDescription: A live customer-success dashboard: charts, tables, and shareable filters that stay in sync with one query cache.
proj-02.fullDescription: Owned the Pulse UI in Next.js—the screen CS uses all day. Charts and tables read from the same TanStack Query cache, filters live in the URL, and role-gated widgets swap density without forking the page. Built for 3G office Wi-Fi: skeletons, prefetch, and no layout jump when data lands.
responsibilities: Designed a single data layer so charts, tables, and KPI tiles never disagree.
Encoded filters and date ranges in the URL so a 30-day customer view is a bookmark, not a screenshot.
Prefetch + skeleton strategy that kept the board usable on slow networks.
Role-gated widgets: managers and agents share one route, different density, zero duplicate pages.

proj-03.title: Commerce Edge
proj-03.shortDescription: Rebuilt the public marketing site on Next.js—Lighthouse 68 → 95, CMS-editable sections, search-ready markup.
proj-03.fullDescription: Tore down a sluggish template site and rebuilt Commerce Edge on the App Router. Route-level splitting, next/image, and subsetted fonts did the performance work; semantic sections and Open Graph tags did the SEO work. Marketing edits copy in a CMS and publishes without waiting on a deploy.
responsibilities: Rebuilt the site as composable Next.js sections from Figma, mobile-first.
Lifted Lighthouse Performance from 68 to 95 via images, fonts, and route splitting.
Shipped structured data, metadata, and OG previews so product pages could rank and share cleanly.
Connected a CMS so campaigns ship as content, not as a frontend ticket.

proj-06.title: Lumen Markets
proj-06.shortDescription: Multi-tenant ecommerce for digital media—one Next.js app, many branded storefronts selling photos, video, audio, and 3D.
proj-06.fullDescription: Lumen is a marketplace platform: each tenant gets a custom domain, catalog, and theme, all from one deploy. Shoppers preview assets, pick a license tier, pay, and download immediately. Tenant isolation is the product—cart, checkout, and SEO never leak across stores. Built the storefront and tenant shell in Next.js so a new brand is config, not a fork.
responsibilities: Resolved tenant from hostname and loaded brand tokens, catalog, and locale without a rebuild.
Shipped PDPs with media preview, license tiers, and post-payment download that never mixed tenant files.
Isolated cart and Stripe checkout per store so two sites on the same app cannot see each other's orders.
Built the merchant publish flow: upload assets, set prices and licenses, go live on a custom domain.

proj-04.title: Flowboard
proj-04.shortDescription: A kanban surface dropped into an existing app—instant card moves, conflict-safe updates, motion that respects reduced-motion.
proj-04.fullDescription: Added Flowboard without rewriting the product. Cards and columns reorder with dnd-kit, Zustand applies the move instantly, and a failed API call rolls the board back. Motion is a 200–400ms ease, not a spectacle; prefers-reduced-motion jumps. The reorder reducer is covered so drag bugs don't ship.
responsibilities: Built card and column drag-and-drop that doesn't fight page scroll or multi-select.
Optimistic Zustand updates with rollback on conflict so moves feel native, not 'saving…'.
Framer Motion transitions that honor reduced-motion instead of ignoring it.
Unit-tested the reorder reducer and edge cases (empty columns, rapid consecutive moves).

proj-05.title: Aperture Docs
proj-05.shortDescription: MDX docs with live examples, keyboard-first search, and a versioned sidebar—engineers publish in Markdown.
proj-05.fullDescription: Aperture is the internal docs site: MDX for guides, live component examples in the page, fuzzy search across headings and body, and a sticky table of contents. Authors add a Markdown file; they don't touch the renderer. Built so onboarding doesn't depend on whoever last remembered how the repo works.
responsibilities: MDX pipeline with custom mapping for callouts, live previews, and typed code blocks.
Fuzzy, keyboard-first search over titles and body—open, type, jump.
Versioned sidebar plus on-page ToC so long guides stay oriented.
Authoring guide that let teammates add pages without changing build config.
